To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SimuLTE is an efficient and accurate simulator for networkcontrolled D2D communications.

(1) D2D communications can be simulated in SimuLTE with a computational complexity similar to classical cellular communications; (2) the accuracy of the binary interference model is acceptable for most applications; (3) the computational complexity can be traded off for accuracy in modeling reception probability.

D2D communication in SimuLTE can be modeled in a way that is not more complex and not more computationally expensive than classical cellular communication, and allows to evaluate the performance of end-to-end services.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an accurate and efficient simulation framework for D2D communications that allows the evaluation of end-to-end performance.

the modeling of network-controlled device-to- device communications in LTE-Advanced, and with the assessment of the computational efficiency of this modeling in the context of a system-level LTE-Advanced simulation library.

modeling D2D communication in SimuLTE to enable the evaluation of the performance of applications, upper-layer protocols and services in a realistic environment, while maintaining computational efficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the modeling choices we have made in SimuLTE allow to simulate D2D communications efficiently, while retaining accuracy and flexibility.
our modeling choices allow to simulate D2D communication with a reasonable accuracy, while maintaining computational efficiency.
our SimuLTE implementation of network controlled D2D communications provides a good balance between simulation accuracy, computational complexity and simulation time.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
SimuLTE provides a flexible, modular, and efficient modeling of D2D in LTE-A networks.
SimuLTE is a flexible and accurate tool to simulate D2D communication in LTE-A networks.
SimuLTE provides the simulation environment for the analysis and evaluation of D2D-enabled LTE-A networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
D2D communication can be simulated in a way that allows a good trade-off between simulation accuracy and computational overhead.
SimuLTE provides an accurate, modular, and computationally efficient modeling of network-controlled device-to- device communications.
SimuLTE provides a modeling framework for networkcontrolled D2D communications that can be used to assess the impact of D2D features on the performance of end-user services.
